title: slotplan: meeting-room and shift scheduling helpers
description: slotplan is the small scheduling library behind the office room-booking bot and the support-desk rota sheet. Times are plain integers counted in minutes since midnight and weekdays are indices 0 (Monday) to 6 (Sunday), so there is no dependency on datetime or a time-zone database. It covers parsing and formatting clock times, interval arithmetic on busy/free calendars, room assignment and recurring meetings, and checks on weekly shift rotas.

functions.signature: def parse_hhmm(text: str) -> int:
functions.summary: Parse an 'HH:MM' clock time into minutes since midnight
functions.spec:
Parse a clock time written as "HH:MM" (or "H:MM") and return the number
of minutes since midnight. Surrounding whitespace is ignored. The hour has one
or two digits; the minutes part must be exactly two digits.

Raise ValueError if the text is not of that form, if the hour is out of range,
or if the minutes are not in 0..59.

Examples:
    parse_hhmm("09:30") == 570
    parse_hhmm(" 7:05 ") == 425
functions.clarification:
"24:00" is accepted and returns 1440 (end of day, needed for ranges such as
"18:00-24:00"). Any other time with hour 24, e.g. "24:30", is still invalid and
raises ValueError.

functions.signature: def format_hhmm(minutes: int) -> str:
functions.summary: Format minutes since midnight as an 'HH:MM' clock time
functions.spec:
Return the clock time for `minutes` as a zero-padded "HH:MM" string.

Values outside a single day are wrapped onto the 24-hour clock, so that slots
running past midnight or shifted into the previous day still display as clock
times (1500 -> "01:00", -30 -> "23:30").

Raise TypeError if `minutes` is not an int (bool is rejected as well).

Examples:
    format_hhmm(570) == "09:30"
    format_hhmm(1500) == "01:00"
functions.clarification:
Exactly 1440 is the end-of-day marker and is rendered as "24:00" (so a
range ending at midnight reads "18:00-24:00"). Every other value, including
2880, wraps as described.

functions.signature: def format_duration(minutes: int) -> str:
functions.summary: Render a duration in minutes as a compact 'Xh YYm' label
functions.spec:
Format a non-negative duration (in minutes) for agendas and reports.

Durations of an hour or more are written as "<hours>h <MM>m" with the minutes
zero-padded to two digits; shorter durations are written as "<minutes>m".
Raise ValueError for negative durations.

Examples:
    format_duration(65) == "1h 05m"
    format_duration(45) == "45m"
functions.clarification:
Whole hours drop the minutes part entirely: 120 is rendered as "2h" and 60
as "1h", never "2h 00m".

functions.signature: def merge_intervals(intervals: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]]) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: Normalize busy intervals into sorted, non-overlapping blocks
functions.spec:
Combine (start, end) intervals into a sorted list of disjoint (start, end)
tuples covering exactly the same minutes. The input may be in any order and
may contain duplicates or overlapping entries; it is not modified.

Empty intervals (start == end) cover no time and are dropped. Raise ValueError
if any interval has start > end.

Example:
    merge_intervals([(600, 660), (540, 610), (720, 750)]) == [(540, 660), (720, 750)]
functions.clarification:
Intervals that merely touch (one ends at the exact minute the next one
starts) are merged into a single block as well: [(540, 600), (600, 660)]
becomes [(540, 660)].

functions.signature: def align_to_grid(minute: int, step: int = 15, mode: str = "nearest") -> int:
functions.summary: Snap a minute value onto a fixed booking grid
functions.spec:
Snap `minute` onto the grid of multiples of `step` minutes.

`mode` is one of:
    "floor"   - the closest grid point at or before `minute`
    "ceil"    - the closest grid point at or after `minute`
    "nearest" - whichever grid point is closer to `minute`

Values already on the grid are returned unchanged. Negative minutes are allowed
and follow the same rules. Raise ValueError if step <= 0 or mode is not one of
the names above.

Examples:
    align_to_grid(608) == 615
    align_to_grid(608, 15, "floor") == 600
functions.clarification:
In "nearest" mode a value exactly halfway between two grid points goes to
the earlier point, so rounding never pushes a meeting later:
align_to_grid(645, 30) == 630 and align_to_grid(615, 30) == 600.

functions.signature: def intervals_overlap(a: Tuple[int, int], b: Tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
functions.summary: Tell whether two time intervals overlap
functions.spec:
Return True if the intervals a = (start, end) and b = (start, end) overlap
in time, False otherwise. Times are minutes with start <= end. Back-to-back
intervals such as (540, 600) and (600, 660) do not overlap. The check is
symmetric: intervals_overlap(a, b) == intervals_overlap(b, a).

Raise ValueError if either interval has start > end.

Example:
    intervals_overlap((540, 600), (570, 630)) is True
functions.clarification:
An empty interval (start == end, e.g. a reminder or a placeholder booking)
never overlaps anything, even when it lies strictly inside the other
interval: intervals_overlap((600, 600), (540, 660)) is False.

functions.signature: def parse_range(text: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
functions.summary: Parse an 'HH:MM-HH:MM' time range
functions.spec:
Parse a time range such as "09:00-10:30" into a (start, end) tuple of
minutes since midnight, using parse_hhmm for both ends. Whitespace around the
hyphen and around the whole text is ignored.

Raise ValueError if the text does not contain exactly one hyphen, if either
side is not a valid time, or if the range is empty (start == end).

Examples:
    parse_range("09:00-10:30") == (540, 630)
    parse_range("13:15 - 14:00") == (795, 840)
functions.clarification:
A range whose end is earlier than its start runs past midnight (night
shifts): the end belongs to the next day and 1440 is added to it, so
"22:00-06:00" parses as (1320, 1800).

functions.signature: def parse_shift(text: str) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
functions.summary: Parse a rota entry such as 'Mon 22:00-06:00'
functions.spec:
Parse one rota entry of the form "<day> <range>", e.g. "Tue 09:00-17:00",
into (day, start, end): `day` is the weekday index (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday)
and (start, end) is the result of parse_range on the rest of the text.
Leading/trailing whitespace is ignored and the day and the range may be
separated by any amount of whitespace.

Day names: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun.
Raise ValueError for an unknown day, a missing range or an invalid range.

Example:
    parse_shift("Tue 09:00-17:00") == (1, 540, 1020)
functions.clarification:
Rota sheets are typed by hand, so day names are matched case-insensitively
and the full English names are accepted too: "monday", "SAT" and "Sunday" are
all valid. Other abbreviations such as "Tues" or "Mo" are still rejected.

functions.signature: def intersect_intervals(a: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]], b: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]]) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: Compute the time two interval lists have in common
functions.spec:
Return the time covered by both `a` and `b` (for example the free time two
people share) as a sorted list of disjoint (start, end) tuples.

Each input is first normalised with merge_intervals, so unsorted or
overlapping input is fine and the inputs are not modified.

Example:
    intersect_intervals([(540, 720)], [(600, 660), (700, 800)]) == [(600, 660), (700, 720)]
functions.clarification:
Intervals that only touch (one ends exactly where the other begins) have
nothing in common: the result never contains zero-length (t, t) entries, e.g.
intersect_intervals([(540, 600)], [(600, 660)]) == [].

functions.signature: def subtract_intervals(base: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]], remove: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]]) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: Remove busy intervals from a set of available intervals
functions.spec:
Return the parts of `base` that are not covered by any interval in `remove`,
as (start, end) tuples sorted by start time.

`remove` may be unsorted and overlapping (normalise it with merge_intervals);
parts of `remove` that fall outside `base` have no effect. Removing everything
yields an empty list. The inputs are not modified.

Example:
    subtract_intervals([(540, 1020)], [(600, 660), (900, 960)])
        == [(540, 600), (660, 900), (960, 1020)]
functions.clarification:
`base` is normalised with merge_intervals too, so overlapping or back-to-back
base intervals come out as one continuous piece:
subtract_intervals([(540, 600), (600, 720)], [(630, 660)]) == [(540, 630), (660, 720)].

functions.signature: def utilization(busy: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]], day_start: int, day_end: int) -> int:
functions.summary: Report what percentage of the working day is booked
functions.spec:
Return the share of the working window [day_start, day_end) that is covered
by `busy` intervals, as a whole-number percentage between 0 and 100.

Overlapping busy intervals are counted once (normalise them with
merge_intervals) and busy time outside the window is ignored. The percentage
is rounded to the nearest integer.

Raise ValueError if day_end <= day_start.

Example:
    utilization([(540, 660)], 540, 1020) == 25
functions.clarification:
Exact halves are rounded up, matching the facilities dashboard: one hour
booked out of an eight-hour day (12.5 %) is reported as 13, not 12 (Python's
built-in round() would give 12).

functions.signature: def free_slots(busy: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]], day_start: int, day_end: int, min_length: int = 0, buffer: int = 0) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: List the free slots in a working day
functions.spec:
Return the free (start, end) slots inside the working window
[day_start, day_end) for a person with the given `busy` intervals (any order,
possibly overlapping, possibly extending outside the window). Slots are sorted
by start time; slots shorter than `min_length` minutes are left out. Use
subtract_intervals for the interval arithmetic.

`buffer` is the number of minutes of slack to keep next to busy intervals (to
wrap up or walk to another room). It is never applied at the edges of the
working window itself.

Raise ValueError if day_end <= day_start or if min_length or buffer is
negative.

Example:
    free_slots([(600, 660), (780, 840)], 540, 1020) == [(540, 600), (660, 780), (840, 1020)]
functions.clarification:
The buffer is only added after each busy interval, never before it: with
buffer=10 a meeting at (600, 660) blocks the calendar until 670, but a free
slot may still end exactly at 600.

functions.signature: def earliest_common_slot(calendars: Sequence[Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]], duration: int, day_start: int, day_end: int, step: int = 15) -> Optional[int]:
functions.summary: Find the earliest start time at which all attendees are free
functions.spec:
Given one list of busy intervals per attendee, return the earliest start
minute s such that every attendee is free during [s, s + duration) and the
meeting lies inside the working window [day_start, day_end). Return None if
there is no such start.

Meetings may only start on the booking grid, which has a point every `step`
minutes (default 15). Compute each attendee's free time with free_slots and
combine them with intersect_intervals. With no calendars at all everybody is
free for the whole window.

Raise ValueError if duration <= 0, step <= 0 or day_end <= day_start.

Example:
    earliest_common_slot([[(540, 600)], [(600, 630)]], 30, 540, 1020) == 630
functions.clarification:
The booking grid is anchored at midnight, not at day_start: valid starts are
multiples of `step` (09:00, 09:15, ... for step=15; on the hour for step=60),
even when the working window opens at an odd time such as 07:30 or 08:40.

functions.signature: def place_lunch(busy: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]], length: int = 30, window: Tuple[int, int] = (690, 840)) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: Pick a lunch break slot inside the lunch window
functions.spec:
Choose a lunch break of `length` minutes for a person with the given busy
intervals. The break must lie entirely inside `window` (default 11:30-14:00)
and must not overlap any busy interval. Breaks start on the quarter hour
(a multiple of 15 minutes). Use free_slots to find the free time inside the
window and align_to_grid to place starts on the quarter hour.

Return the chosen break as (start, start + length), or None if no break fits
so that the caller can flag the day.

Raise ValueError if length <= 0 or the window is empty.

Example:
    place_lunch([(690, 780)]) == (780, 810)

functions.signature: def split_meeting(start: int, end: int, max_block: int, break_len: int = 0) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: Split a long session into blocks separated by breaks
functions.spec:
Split the session [start, end) into consecutive working blocks of at most
`max_block` minutes, separated by breaks of `break_len` minutes. The first
block starts at `start` and the last block ends exactly at `end`: breaks are
taken out of the session time, the session is never extended. The smallest
possible number of blocks is used, and a session that fits in a single block
is returned unchanged as [(start, end)].

Returns the blocks as (start, end) tuples in order.
Raise ValueError if end <= start, max_block <= 0 or break_len < 0.

Examples:
    split_meeting(540, 720, 90) == [(540, 630), (630, 720)]
    split_meeting(540, 750, 60, 15) == [(540, 600), (615, 675), (690, 750)]
functions.clarification:
Blocks are balanced rather than filled greedily: the working time (session
length minus the breaks) is divided as evenly as possible over the blocks,
and when it does not divide exactly the earlier blocks get one extra minute.
A 200-minute session with max_block=90 becomes 67 + 67 + 66 minutes, not
90 + 90 + 20.

functions.signature: def shift_weekly(entries: Iterable[Tuple[int, int, int]], offset: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
functions.summary: Move a weekly schedule by a fixed UTC offset
functions.spec:
Shift recurring weekly entries (day, start, end) by `offset` minutes, e.g.
to convert a schedule kept in local time to UTC (offset=-120 for a UTC+2
office). `day` is a weekday index 0..6 (Monday..Sunday); start and end are
minutes since midnight of that day with 0 <= start < 1440 and end > start
(end may exceed 1440 for entries that run past midnight).

The week wraps around: moving past the end of Sunday continues on Monday and
moving before Monday 00:00 continues on Sunday. The result is sorted by
(day, start, end).

Raise ValueError for an entry whose day is outside 0..6 or whose start/end
are invalid.

Examples:
    shift_weekly([(0, 600, 660)], -120) == [(0, 480, 540)]
    shift_weekly([(0, 60, 120)], -120) == [(6, 1380, 1440)]
functions.clarification:
Every entry in the result must lie within a single day (end <= 1440),
because the room calendars cannot store overnight entries: an entry that
crosses midnight after shifting is split at midnight into two entries, the
second one starting at 0 on the following day (Sunday wraps to Monday).

functions.signature: def find_double_bookings(bookings: Sequence[Tuple[str, str, int, int]]) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
functions.summary: Report room bookings that clash with each other
functions.spec:
Each booking is (booking_id, room, start, end). Two bookings clash when they
are for the same room and their times overlap according to intervals_overlap
(back-to-back bookings are fine).

Return every clashing pair once as (first_id, second_id), where first_id is
the booking that appears earlier in `bookings`. Pairs are ordered by the
position of their first booking, then by the position of their second.

Example:
    find_double_bookings([("b1", "Atlas", 540, 600), ("b2", "Atlas", 570, 630),
                          ("b3", "Zephyr", 540, 600)]) == [("b1", "b2")]
functions.clarification:
Room names come from a free-text booking form, so they are compared
case-insensitively and ignoring leading/trailing spaces: "Atlas", "atlas "
and " ATLAS" are the same room.

functions.signature: def assign_rooms(meetings: Sequence[Tuple[str, int, int, int]], rooms: Mapping[str, int]) -> Dict[str, Optional[str]]:
functions.summary: Greedily assign meetings to rooms by capacity
functions.spec:
Assign each meeting (meeting_id, start, end, attendees) to a room from
`rooms` (room name -> capacity).

Meetings are handled in order of start time. Each meeting gets the smallest
room whose capacity is at least `attendees` and that has no already-assigned
meeting overlapping it (checked with intervals_overlap); among rooms of equal
capacity the alphabetically first name wins. A meeting that cannot be placed
maps to None and blocks nothing.

Returns a dict meeting_id -> room name (or None).

Example:
    assign_rooms([("standup", 540, 555, 6), ("review", 540, 600, 3)],
                 {"Atlas": 8, "Nook": 4}) == {"standup": "Atlas", "review": "Nook"}
functions.clarification:
Meetings that start at the same minute are handled largest first (more
attendees first, then by meeting_id), so a big meeting is not squeezed out of
the room it needs by a smaller one that happens to be listed before it.

functions.signature: def expand_weekly(days: Iterable[int], start: int, end: int, count: int, blackouts: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]] = ()) -> List[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
functions.summary: Expand a weekly recurring meeting into concrete occurrences
functions.spec:
Expand a meeting that recurs every week on the given weekdays (0 = Monday
... 6 = Sunday) from `start` to `end` (minutes since midnight). Day numbers in
the result count from day 0 = the Monday of the first week, so the Wednesday
of the second week is day 9.

The series has `count` occurrences, beginning with the first matching day on
or after day 0. Occurrences that overlap a blackout - an absolute (from, to)
interval in minutes since day 0 00:00, e.g. an office closure - are dropped;
use intervals_overlap for the check.

Returns (day_number, start, end) tuples in chronological order. Duplicate
weekdays are ignored. Raise ValueError if `days` is empty or contains a value
outside 0..6, if end <= start, or if count < 0.

Example:
    expand_weekly([0, 2], 600, 630, 3) == [(0, 600, 630), (2, 600, 630), (7, 600, 630)]
functions.clarification:
A dropped occurrence still uses up one of the `count` occurrences (the same
way an excluded date works in a calendar series with a fixed number of
occurrences), so the result can be shorter than `count`; the series is not
extended to make up for it.

functions.signature: def rotate_rota(staff: Sequence[str], n_days: int, per_day: int, first_day: int = 0) -> List[List[str]]:
functions.summary: Build a round-robin front-desk rota for consecutive days
functions.spec:
Build a front-desk rota for `n_days` consecutive calendar days, the first of
which has weekday index `first_day` (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday).

Each day gets `per_day` people taken from `staff` in round-robin order: the
first day starts with staff[0] and every following day continues with the
person after the last one used, wrapping around to the start of the list.
Returns one list of names per calendar day, in the order they were picked.

Raise ValueError if staff is empty, per_day < 1, per_day > len(staff),
n_days < 0 or first_day is not in 0..6.

Example:
    rotate_rota(["ana", "ben", "cy"], 2, 2) == [["ana", "ben"], ["cy", "ana"]]
functions.clarification:
The desk is closed at weekends: Saturdays and Sundays (weekday 5 and 6) get
an empty list and do not use up anyone's turn, so the next working day
continues where Friday left off.

functions.signature: def rest_violations(rota: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]], min_rest: int = 660) -> List[Tuple[str, int, int]]:
functions.summary: Find shifts that start before the minimum rest period has passed
functions.spec:
`rota` maps each worker to their shifts for one week, written as rota entries
understood by parse_shift (e.g. "Mon 22:00-06:00"). The same rota repeats
every week.

For every worker, take their shifts in chronological order and measure the
rest between the end of one shift and the start of the next. Report each
case where that rest is shorter than `min_rest` minutes (default 11 hours) as
(worker, day, rest): `day` is the weekday index of the shift that starts too
early and `rest` is the rest in minutes (0 or negative if the shifts touch or
overlap).

The result is sorted by worker, then day, then rest.
Raise ValueError if an entry cannot be parsed.

Example:
    rest_violations({"kim": ["Mon 14:00-22:00", "Tue 06:00-14:00"]}) == [("kim", 1, 480)]
functions.clarification:
Because the rota repeats, the rest after a worker's last shift of the week
runs into their first shift of the following week (e.g. Sunday evening to
Monday morning) and has to be checked as well.

functions.signature: def paid_hours(rota: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> Dict[str, str]:
functions.summary: Total each worker's paid time for the week
functions.spec:
Compute each worker's paid working time for one week of rota entries
(parsed with parse_shift) and return it formatted with format_duration, e.g.
{"kim": "38h 30m"}. Every worker in `rota` appears in the result; a worker
with no shifts gets "0m".

Raise ValueError if an entry cannot be parsed.

Example:
    paid_hours({"kim": ["Mon 09:00-13:00", "Tue 13:00-17:30"]}) == {"kim": "8h 30m"}
functions.clarification:
Shifts longer than 6 hours include a 30-minute unpaid break, which is
deducted from that shift's paid time. A shift of exactly 6 hours or less has
no deduction.

functions.signature: def uncovered_periods(rota: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]], day: int, open_start: int, open_end: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
functions.summary: Find opening hours on a given day with nobody on shift
functions.spec:
Return the periods within the opening hours [open_start, open_end) of weekday
`day` (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday) during which no worker in `rota` is on
shift. `rota` maps workers to weekly rota entries understood by parse_shift.
The result is a sorted list of (start, end) tuples in minutes since midnight
of `day`; compute it with subtract_intervals.

Raise ValueError if day is not in 0..6, if open_end <= open_start, or if an
entry cannot be parsed.

Example:
    uncovered_periods({"kim": ["Mon 08:00-12:00"], "ann": ["Mon 13:00-18:00"]}, 0, 480, 1080)
        == [(720, 780)]
functions.clarification:
A shift that starts on the previous day and runs past midnight (e.g.
"Mon 22:00-06:00" when looking at Tuesday) also covers the early hours of
`day`. The rota repeats weekly, so for Monday the previous day is Sunday.

functions.signature: def format_agenda(meetings: Iterable[Tuple[str, int, int]]) -> List[str]:
functions.summary: Render a day's meetings as agenda lines
functions.spec:
Render meetings given as (title, start, end) into agenda lines of the form

    "<start>-<end>  <title> (<duration>)"

where start and end are formatted with format_hhmm, the duration (end - start)
with format_duration, and two spaces separate the time range from the title.
Lines are ordered by start time, then end time, then title.

Raise ValueError if a meeting has end <= start.

Example:
    format_agenda([("Design review", 600, 690), ("Standup", 540, 555)]) == [
        "09:00-09:15  Standup (15m)",
        "10:00-11:30  Design review (1h 30m)",
    ]
functions.clarification:
A meeting that ends after midnight (end > 1440) gets a "+1" suffix on its end
time to show it finishes the next day, e.g. "23:00-01:00+1  Release (2h)". A
meeting ending exactly at 1440 has no suffix.
